title: CPTAC AML Study
summary:
Lipidomics is the scarcest measurement type in the entire corpus indexed here: three studies carry it, all within CPTAC, and this is the largest. Combined with metabolomics on the same 98 patients and four proteomic layers on all 164, it supports metabolic questions in leukaemia that cannot be posed anywhere else with measured rather than inferred data.
AML is a disease where metabolic state has clear therapeutic relevance, and where measured lipid and metabolite data on primary patient samples are close to unobtainable. The barrier to reuse here is discoverability rather than access: everything is open, and nothing about the PDC catalog entry tells a metabolism researcher that this cohort exists.
one_liner: 164 acute myeloid leukaemias with proteome, phosphoproteome, acetylome and glycoproteome, plus lipidomics and metabolomics on 98 - one of only three NCI cohorts carrying lipidomic data, openly downloadable.

useful_for.question: How does lipid composition differ across AML subtypes, and does it relate to differentiation state?
useful_for.rationale: Lipidomic profiles on 98 primary AML samples, alongside proteome on all 164, allow lipid class abundance to be related to protein markers of myeloid differentiation on the same patients. Measured lipidomics on primary AML at this scale is essentially unavailable elsewhere.
useful_for.statistical_note: 98 samples supports class-level comparison and well-powered subgroup contrasts only for common subtypes; rare fusion subgroups will have single-digit counts.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Do measured metabolite levels agree with metabolic state inferred from transcript or protein abundance?
useful_for.rationale: Metabolomics and proteomics on the same 98 patients allow a direct test of an assumption that a large body of computational metabolic modeling depends on and rarely gets to check.
useful_for.statistical_note: This is a methods-validation design; effect sizes are the quantity of interest, not significance.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Does protein acetylation, a modification tightly coupled to metabolic cofactor availability, track measured metabolite levels?
useful_for.rationale: Acetylome on 164 cases and metabolome on 98 overlap substantially. Acetylation depends on acetyl-CoA availability, so this cohort can test a mechanistic link that is usually assumed rather than measured.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Can glycoproteomic features stratify AML in ways expression cannot?
useful_for.rationale: Glycoproteome on all 164 cases; cell-surface glycosylation is directly relevant to immunotherapy target selection in myeloid disease.

limitations.statement: No clinical annotation is distributed with the PDC study: no survival, no treatment, no cytogenetic risk group, no demographics.
limitations.mitigation: Cytogenetic risk group is essential context in AML. Obtain the matching clinical data from the GDC CPTAC records or the CPTAC data portal before drawing any clinical conclusion.

limitations.statement: Lipidome and metabolome cover 98 cases while the proteomic layers cover 164, so the metabolic analyses run on 60% of the cohort.
limitations.mitigation: Report the overlap explicitly and check whether the 98 differ systematically from the rest.
